headlines.title: Gabby Williams leads Valkyries to WNBA championship in second season, beating Dream 68-63 in Game 7
headlines.description: Gabby Williams scored her team’s final 11 points of the third quarter and dazzled through the fourth on the way to 30 points, and the Golden State Valkyries captured a championship in just their second season by beating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in a sensational first WNBA Finals Game 7 on Saturday night. Jordin Canada scored 18 points, Allisha Gray 16 and Angel Reese had eight points and 12 rebounds for the Dream, denied another championship in the franchise’s fourth try. Gray made two free throws with 11 seconds left then Atlanta forced a jump ball — Gray against Williams — and Veronica Burton corralled it and converted two free throws with 5.1 seconds to go. “I’m just so blessed, this is insane!” said Burton, cut by Dallas two years ago. Rhyne Howard’s layup tied it at 57 with 2:41 left only for Williams to answer once more with a clutch 3-pointer. She converted two free throws with 1:40 remaining, then Kiah Stokes scored a late basket. Stokes pulled down 13 rebounds and blocked two more shots to cap her spectacular postseason. Williams left Seattle with a great feeling about joining Golden State and its close-knit culture, returning to the Bay Area where she played youth basketball to build something special with the Valkyries — and she’s now done that. Fans chanted “Gabby! Gabby!” throughout the fourth quarter. “All it took was good people,” she said. “All we heard last year was we don’t have no stars. We don’t have no talent. Yeah right! We got good people. We got good people. We got winners. We got people who are ready to put their bodies on the floor to win a game.” When the final buzzer sounded, the violet-clad sellout crowd at Chase Center went into a frenzy as players sprinted onto the floor to hug and celebrate as confetti fell from the rafters. “Ballhalla” had become “Boohalla” for this far-but-haunted Halloween night in the raucous arena. Now, with a women’s championship to its name right alongside the one earned by the Golden State Warriors in 2022. “We gotta build a bigger trophy case,” co-owner Peter Guber said. The team that led at halftime in the first six matchups had won every game so far, and the Dream were ahead 30-24 at the break. Atlanta also had been 16-0 this season when Reese made at least one 3. The Dream’s DeWanna Bonner became the first player in WNBA history to reach 600 career postseason defensive rebounds. Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase changed her starting lineup in a move that paid huge dividends after Golden State fell behind 2-1, inserting Kaila Charles and Tiffany Hayes and bringing Kayla Thornton and Cecilia Zandalasini off the bench. The 37-year-old Hayes, who came out of retirement two years ago and spent 10 seasons with the Dream, scored 11 points in the winner-take-all Game 7 and brought energy all series that made Nakase want to win for the veteran guard as much as anybody. Valkyries owner Joe Lacob guaranteed a championship within the first five years for this franchise three years ago when the Bay Area was granted an expansion team, and in improbable, joyful fashion, his team accomplished it in Year 2. That after becoming the first expansion organization to reach the playoffs in its inaugural year in 2025. During the victory ceremony, Lacob shouted out the team and its leaders, while Nakase, general manager Ohemma Nyanin and President Jess Smith hugged. And Lacob thanked the fans who have sold out Chase Center for every game since Day 1. “Ballhalla!” Lacob hollered. ___ See AP’s full WNBA coverage here WNBA Oct 30 Golden State Valkyries Oct 30 Nakase and Valkyries are determined to avoid another slow start in WNBA Finals Game 7 against Dream

headlines.title: Pregnant woman killed in shooting that left other 6 hurt at Halloween store in Fairfield
headlines.description: A pregnant woman was killed in a shooting that left other six people hurt inside the Spirit Halloween store at the Solano Town Center in Fairfield on Friday night, police said Saturday. Police identified the victim as 31-year-old Constance Hages. Authorities said Hages’ family told detectives she was pregnant at the time of her death, but police said the information will be confirmed following an examination by the Solano County Coroner. Fairfield police said it is believed the shooting stemmed from a “targeted incident” involving one suspect inside the Spirit Halloween Store. On Friday, officers responded to a shooting inside the Solano Town Center at the Spirit Halloween store at 8:30 p.m., according to authorities. Seven people were shot and one of them died. Authorities reported that the victims who remain in critical condition are a 16-year-old boy, a 19-year-old man and a 32-year-old man. Officials said a 23-year-old man remains hospitalized “in critical but stable condition,” while a 19-year-old man and a 43-year-old man received treatment for gunshot wounds and have since been released from the hospital. “Fairfield’s greatest strength is how we all look out for each other. I urge everyone in our community to support one another in this obviously very troubled time, especially now,” Fairfield Mayor Rick Vaccaro said on Saturday. “Obviously, it’s going to be on everybody’s mind when an incident like this occurs, and I know it will always be on my mind for a long time.” Spirit Halloween released a statement regarding the shooting: “We are deeply saddened by the tragic incident that occurred inside of the Solano Town Center at the Spirit Halloween store in Fairfield, CA. Our thoughts and prayers are with the families of the victims of this heartbreaking incident. We are fully cooperating with local law enforcement as they investigate the circumstances surrounding this event. As this remains an active investigation, we defer to the Fairfield Police Department for further details. Out of respect for those impacted and to support the ongoing investigation, the store will remain closed until further notice.” Solano Town Center’s planned Halloween trick-or-treating event was cancelled following the incident, according to the mall’s website. Fairfield police said this is an ongoing investigation. They ask anyone with information to contact them at 707-428-7600 or email 1030mall@fairfield.ca.gov.

headlines.title: 1 dead, 6 hurt following shooting at Solano Town Center in Fairfield
headlines.description: One person died and six others were hurt following a shooting at the Solano Town Center in Fairfield on Friday night, according to police. Officers responded to a shooting inside the Solano Town Center at the Spirit Halloween store at 8:30 p.m., authorities said. Fairfield police said seven people were shot and one of them died. The other six victims were taken to the hospital, and three of them are in critical condition. Police said the suspect has not been identified. This is an ongoing investigation. Suisun City mayor Alma Hernandez released a statement regarding the incident. “Our thoughts are with the City of Fairfield tonight. Reports of an active shooter at Solano Town Center (Fairfield Mall) have left multiple victims. Law enforcement is actively searching for the suspect. Our Suisun City Police Department is supporting the search through mutual aid. “Although this happened in Fairfield, it is close to our community, so please stay alert and use official sources for the latest information. For updates, follow the Fairfield, CA Police Department on Facebook and the City of Fairfield’s official websites and social media accounts. Please avoid sharing unverified posts, which can spread confusion and hinder the response. “Please join us in praying for the victims and their families, and for the officers working to bring the suspect into custody. “Once this incident is resolved, we will need to come together as a community to support each other, the victims, and everyone affected by this tragedy. We will refer to the City of Fairfield Police Department to share more information as it becomes available.”

headlines.title: Bay Area voter guide: What to know about the November 2026 election
headlines.description: What to Know — Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026 California will choose a new governor to replace Gavin Newsom, who terms out after this year. The choices are Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton. Voters will decide 14 state propositions. Regional sales tax Measure RTM, the Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, aims to increase funds for public transit. California’s Congressional District 11 race features Scott Wiener and Connie Chan competing to succeed Nancy Pelosi. Aisha Wahab and Melissa Hernandez will face off again after a special election in August where Wahab secured victory to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. All 80 California Assembly seats are up for reelection, as well as 20 Senate seats. California’s general election is Nov. 3, with statewide races and propositions as well as key local races and measures across the Bay Area. Here’s what you need to know to cast your ballot, including important dates and deadlines, how to register or check your status, where and when to vote, and what’s on the ballot. In this guide: Key election dates Check voter registration status How to register to vote How to find your polling place What to bring to your polling place How to track your mail-in ballot Why is California choosing a new governor? 14 California propositions What to watch Alameda County What to watch Contra Costa County What to watch Napa County What to watch San Francisco What to watch San Mateo County What to watch Santa Clara County What to watch Solano County County election offices Key election dates The last day to register to vote for the Nov. 3 general election is Oct. 19. County election officials will start mailing ballots by Oct. 5. Ballot drop-off locations open on Oct. 6 Last day to register to vote for the general election is Oct. 19. First vote centers open for early in-person voting in all Voter’s Choice Act counties on Oct. 24. In person early voting locations in the state open on Oct. 31. Election Day, Nov. 3, is the last day to vote in-person or return a ballot by 8 p.m. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Vote-by-mail ballots must be postmarked no later than Nov. 3. If mailing on election day, get a hand-stamped postmark from a postal employee inside a post office. Visit the California Secretary of State’s website for a full list of key dates and deadlines. Check voter registration status Voters can check their registration at voterstatus.sos.ca.gov to confirm their mailing address and voting status. How to register to vote California residents can register to vote in elections at registertovote.ca.gov. Note Oct. 19 is the last day to register for the general election. Same day voter registration window will be open from Oct. 20 up to the Nov. 3 election day. Visit caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov for a list of early voting locations to complete same day registration. How to find your polling place Visit the California Secretary of State’s website, where you can input your address to find your polling location and see what is on your ballot. Voters can also visit their county elections office for more information. Scroll down to the Bay Area county election offices section of this guide for further contact information. What to bring to your polling place Voters usually are not required to show identification to a polling place worker before casting a ballot, according to the Secretary of State’s website. There are some instances when providing identification is required: Voting for the first time after registering to vote by mail and did not provide a driver license number California identification number or the last four digits of social security number are missing on registration form In these cases voters should plan to bring identification to a polling place or bring a copy of it with their vote-by-mail ballot. The Secretary of State says the following are acceptable forms of identification: Passport Driver license Official state identification card Student identification card Copy of recent utility bill Sample ballot booklet received from county elections office Any document received by a government agency How to track your mail-in ballot Voters can track their vote-by-mail ballot and confirm it has been received by using the state’s Where’s My Ballot? tool at california.ballottrax.net/voter/. Ballots mailed in may take a few days to appear on the website. Why is California choosing a new governor? Gov. Gavin Newsom terms out after this year and voters will choose between Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton, who both advanced to the general election after a wild primary. Becerra has served as former President Joe Biden’s top health official and oversaw the response to the coronavirus pandemic. He was also the California’s attorney general during President Donald Trump’s first term and has more than two decades of experience as a congressmember. Hilton was a conservative commentator with a show on Fox News for six years. He also worked as an adviser to former British prime minister David Cameron. What are the 14 California propositions voters will decide in the November election? Here’s a list of the California propositions on the November ballot. Use the expandable graphic below for a breakdown on what to know about each measure. 2026 California Ballot Propositions Click on a proposition to see more information about what will happen if it does or doesn’t pass. Source: NBC Staff Reports • Interactive: Annetta Stogniew Regional measure to watch Measure RTM: The Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, is a regional sales tax aimed at increasing funds for public transit. It includes 5 Bay Area counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara. Races and measures to watch in Alameda County California Congressional District 14: California lawmaker Aisha Wahab and Bay Area Rapid Transit Director Melissa Hernandez will face off again to determine who will serve the next full two-year term. Wahab topped Hernandez in an August special election to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. Swalwell resigned from Congress earlier this year after sexual assault and misconduct allegations. District 14 includes the East Bay cities such as Fremont, Hayward and Livermore. Measure X in Berkeley: Would establish 10% limit on annual rent increases and other changes to the city’s rent ordinance. Measure Y in Berkeley: Parcel tax to pay for arts projects. Measure Z in Berkeley: Parcel tax to fund a public bank. Measure AA in Berkeley: Increase soda tax Measure EE in Oakland: Shift city to a strong mayor system. Measure FF in Oakland: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Alameda County and additional election information, visit the Alameda County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Contra Costa County In Contra Costa County, several county board of education seats are open. In Richmond, residents will vote on a new mayor while voters in San Pablo will weigh in on Measure S, which would limit rent increases. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Contra Costa County and additional election information, visit the Contra Costa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Napa County California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. Measure B in Napa County: Sales tax to fund wildfire prevention and open space preservation. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Napa County and additional election information, visit the Napa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Francisco San Francisco voters will weigh in on several open seats on the county board of supervisors and board of education. Proposition A: Give mayor more power to hire and fire department heads. Proposition B: Pave way for public bank. Proposition C: Increase the city’s annual contribution to an affordable housing trust fund. Proposition D: New barriers to placing measures on the ballot. Proposition E: Changes to city contracting. Proposition G: Reopen parts of the Great Highway to vehicle traffic on weekdays. Proposition H: Parcel tax to fund Muni. Proposition J: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax California Congressional District 11: Scott Wiener and Connie Chan compete to succeed Nancy Pelosi. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Francisco and additional election information, visit the San Francisco Department of Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Mateo County Measure E in Redwood City: Limit rent increases. Measure Q in Half Moon Bay: Referendum to block proposed farmworker housing. Measure U in San Mateo County: Create independent commission to draw supervisor districts. For a complete list of San Mateo County measures and races on the ballot, visit smacre.gov/elections. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Mateo County and additional election information, visit the San Mateo County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Santa Clara County In San Jose, incumbents Peter Ortiz and Bien Doan are up for re-election in Districts 5 and 7, respectively, and there’s an open seat in District 9. Races and measures to watch in Solano County Solano County Board of Supervisors, District 4: Mike Silva and John Carli face in a runoff in a district covering Vacaville and Dixon. Measure E in Solano County: New tax on data centers and battery storage facilities in the unincorporated county areas. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Solano County and additional election information, visit the Solano County Registrar of Voters website. Races and measures to watch in Sonoma County California Congressional District 1: Mike McGuire will face James Gallagher in a seat redistricted by Proposition 50. California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. State Assembly District 12: Eric Lucan and Jackie Elward compete in a battle between business and labor. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Sonoma County and additional election information, visit the Sonoma County Registrar of Voters website. headlines.title: East Palo Alto tenants worry about safety, smells after apartments flooded
headlines.description: Residents of an East Palo Alto apartment complex are expressing concerns about the safety of their building and communication with their property management after recent flooding waterlogged their apartments. When storms hit on October 22, residents at the Woodland Park Apartments at 430 East O’Keefe Street said they began noticing water pouring into their homes. Rachel Anderson, who has lived in that apartment complex for five years, said the issues escalated by October 23. “The roof caved through — the roof that they’ve been fixin’ on for the last couple of months — so it finally caved through,” Anderson said. “And when it came through, all the water was coming through, and it was coming through the walls,” she continued. Tenants said this left their walls and floors soaked. The property owner vacated residents from their homes. East Palo Alto Mayor Webster Lincoln said that the city red-tagged all 58 units in that building. He said that city crews have worked every day since on repairs. Now, more than a week later, Lincoln said that 50 of those units have now been cleared for residents to return to. Eight other units still need permitted repairs, and Lincoln said those repairs may take longer than a week to complete. Some tenants said they’re worried about going back to their apartments, they expressed worries about a lingering odor, which they say smells like mold. “If he thinks we’re [gonna] move back into this building because he came in here did some carpet cleaning, just patched up the walls, that’s not gonna work for me at all,” Rachel Anderson said of the property owner. The mayor said he toured the building Thursday after the red tags came down and noticed a strong odor. “I will be asking City staff to require moisture readings or air quality testing before residents move back,” he said. While the units were red-tagged, the property owner put tenants up in hotel rooms. At first, the tenants said they were assigned to stay at a hotel in Palo Alto. But after the first few days, tenants said they were relocated to another hotel in San Mateo, which is a 14-mile, 19-minute drive away from their apartments. Anderson said this distance is particularly difficult for the tenants who do not have cars and need to get to their jobs in Palo Alto. Other tenants said that the extra cost of gas to drive to and from their jobs and their kids’ schools has been eating into their budgets for rent. Tenants are being asked to pay rent like normal at the start of the month in November. The mayor explained that technically, that is allowed under municipal code. He said that landlords must pay for temporary housing within 15 miles, plus moving and storage costs. However, the mayor is now urging the property owner to do more. “I am calling on Sand Hill to give residents a rent credit for the time they have been displaced,” Lincoln said. “I also want a per diem for meals and travel, and housing closer to East Palo Alto so children can get to school and parents can get to work, ” he continued. “Residents also deserve clear, consistent communication about where they are going and when they can return.” Roberto Arias, who lives at a Woodland Park apartment across the street managed by the same owner, said he wants to see his neighbor’s concerns taken seriously. “Because these people pay a lot of rent for a damaged apartment, I really want to know whats going on, I hope the person who owns this building is looking at this interview, because you need to be here,” Arias said. NBC Bay Area has reached out to the listed owners for this property, but we have not received a response yet. The mayor added that any tenants who’ve been impacted by this can contact the City’s Community and Economic Development Department at CED@cityofepa.org or Community Legal Services in East Palo Alto at (650) 326-6440 for free help. “Please do not sign anything that waives your relocation rights before getting advice,” Lincoln said.

headlines.title: Sheriff's office restricts access to South Bay jail following ICE activity
headlines.description: ICE officers have maintained a constant presence this week, especially around Santa Clara County’s jail facilities, apparently waiting to question people about their immigration status right after they’re released. This has led to some physical confrontations caught on camera. NBC Bay Area was inside the Elmwood facility on Friday before the sheriff’s office announced that access to the parking lot and lobby would be restricted to people with direct business at the facility. The restrictions come as a response to the increased ICE activity, including an incident in which officers used a taser. Liz Gonzalez was shooting video of a man released from the Elmwood jail who tried to elude ICE officers by hiding in a nearby creek. He ran and green lights from tasers were aimed right at him. “Obviously I was in fear. I was shocked. I was surprised and scared by what I saw. I was so scared for those individuals because I thought that they were going to kill them,” Gonzalez said. Gonzalez is with the watchdog group Silicon Valley De-Bug, which has been videotaping ICE officers since Sunday when they showed up at Elmwood, capturing encounters with people being released. The Rapid Response Network in Santa Clara County says ICE officers have been very assertive. Top Santa Clara County leaders said on Friday they are very concerned about the escalation in activity, stating, “The county continues to uphold its long-standing non-cooperation policies regarding federal civil immigration enforcement. With Election Day next week, we are committed to ensuring all citizens are able to freely and safely cast their vote.” “Well, it’s no coincidence that we’ve seen a larger ICE presence right before the elections, so this is very consistent with what we’re seeing up and down the state of California,” Rapid Response Network coordinator Jeremy Barousse said. For now, groups say the immigrant community is on edge. “People are afraid. Both family members outside, and we’re hearing that the people detained inside also very afraid. Even folks who are ‘not at risk.’ Everybody’s at risk, and especially people who look Latino, obviously we know that,” Gonzalez said.

headlines.title: Man accused of breaking into Oakland Police Officer's Association building
headlines.description: A man broke into the Oakland Police Officer’s Association building last month, officials confirmed on Saturday. Investigators say the man stole money from a cabinet. He was caught nearby, allegedly attempting another burglary. According to court documents, the suspect was on probation from burglary convictions last year in Contra Costa County. “This demonstrates, sadly, that no one, not even police officers, is immune to ongoing crime in Oakland,” OPOA spokesman Sam Singer said.

headlines.title: Star witness in Sheng Thao corruption trial details alleged bribery scheme
headlines.description: The star prosecution witness in the federal corruption trial of former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao testified Friday about his role in an alleged scheme to funnel money to her in exchange for political favors. Mario Juarez, a long-time Oakland political operative and former City Council candidate, testified about how he allegedly managed a pay-to-play relationship between Thao, her romantic partner Andre Jones, and David and Andy Duong, a father-son duo who operate the city’s recycling contractor, California Waste Solutions. Thao, Jones and the Duongs all pleaded not guilty to a rash of federal corruption and bribery charges in January. Juarez is testifying for the U.S. Department of Justice after pleading guilty to a bribery conspiracy charge of his own. In court on Friday, Juarez detailed the accusations at the heart of the prosecution’s case — that the Duongs allegedly agreed to pay Jones $300,000 a year for a fake job in exchange for Thao’s help securing a city contract to purchase modular homes. The homes were to be built by a company called Evolutionary Homes, founded by Juarez and the Duongs to build modular housing units out of old shipping containers with the intention of selling them to local governments to help with homelessness issues. Sheng Thao Oct 29 Sheng Thao Oct 28 The alleged quid pro quo agreement also involved Thao helping the family win a 10-year extension for their existing recycling contract, an extension of their existing land-lease at the old Oakland army base and an alleged promise from Thao to place their hand-picked candidate in a high-level position inside city government. Juarez also told the jury that as part of the illicit agreement, he helped the Duongs spend $75,000 on last-minute negative campaign mailers to help Thao win a tight mayoral election in 2022. He also said that he illegally coordinated with Jones to design the mailers. The original agreement only included using an independent expenditure committee to produce the negative mailers and to help Thao get elected, Juarez said, but Thao allegedly had an additional demand. “Then she threw a curveball,” he said. “We were willing to do the campaign and all the things in exchange, but she said, ‘I want $300,000 in exchange.'” The defendants were then thrust into a position in which they had to figure out a way to make payments to Jones look legitimate, Juarez said. To do that, they allegedly created a fake, no-show job for Jones so the payments wouldn’t arouse suspicion, Juarez said. During the day’s testimony, lead prosecutor Assistant U.S. Attorney Abraham Fine showed the jury images of checks written to Jones that were allegedly in exchange for Thao’s part in the conspiracy. The jury also saw dozens of text messages between the defendants that prosecutors say are evidence of their long-running effort to pull off the scheme. In one such exchange after Thao eked out a narrow win in the mayoral election, Juarez texted Andy Duong “so we may go to jail.” “I was making light that we just committed a crime by funding an election and we may go to jail for doing this crime, but we’ll have $100 million in our bank account,” Jaurez told the jury Friday. Juarez also testified that the payments to Jones were going to increase to a total of up to $3 million, based on how many modular homes Oakland agreed to buy, “in exchange” for Thao’s agreement to help with the Duongs’ list of requests. “In exchange, the compensation went from $300,000 to a structure that would now make them millionaires,” Juarez said. He also testified about how he and Andy Duong planned their communications between themselves and other people involved in the alleged conspiracy in order to protect Andy’s father, David, and so that the elder Duong would have “plausible deniability” in the event that law enforcement started poking around. Juarez also said that he and Andy Duong became frustrated as the deal started to fall apart and when it appeared as of Thao wasn’t holding up her part of the bargain. “We didn’t invest money, talent, (negative political) ‘hits,’ took the time out of our day because we liked Sheng Thao,” he said, adding that they did all those things so that she would help them execute the scheme to further their business interests. Juarez testified for several hours Friday and is expected to be back on the stand when the trial resumes Thursday.

headlines.title: 2 San Jose women allegedly stabbed person to death, dumped body in rural Alameda County
headlines.description: Two San Jose women were arrested earlier this week on suspicion of killing a person whose body was found in August off the side of a rural road in eastern Alameda County, police said Friday. Alexia Nieves Solache, 22, and Veronica Rangel, 55, allegedly stabbed the unidentified victim to death at a home in San Jose before dumping their body in the area of Tesla and Eagles Run roads outside Livermore, according to police. Alameda County Sheriff’s Office deputies initially responded at about 3:04 p.m. on Aug. 25 to the area of Tesla and Eagles Run roads to investigate a report of a possible deceased person, San Jose police said. The reporting party said he was driving when he spotted what appeared to be a concealed person in a ravine. Responding sheriff’s deputies found the person and determined they were dead. The victim had suffered multiple stab wounds, and their manner of death was ruled a homicide, according to police. Deputies determined the victim was last seen on Aug. 22 at a home on the 700 block of North Seventh Street in San Jose. The home did not belong to the victim, police said. Deputies also identified a suspect vehicle that was seen traveling from the home in San Jose to the location outside Livermore where the victim was found. Investigators determined the homicide happened at the home in San Jose, and they identified Solache and Rangel as the primary suspects, police said. Both suspects were arrested on Tuesday – Solache in Los Angeles and Rangel in San Jose, according to police. They were eventually booked into the Santa Clara County Main Jail on suspicion of murder. The motive and circumstances surrounding the homicide – San Jose’s 24th of 2026 – remain under investigation, police said. Anyone with information is asked to contact San Jose police Detective Sgt. Varela and/or Detective Montoya by email at 3638@sanjoseca.gov and/or 3644@sanjoseca.gov or by phone at 408-277-5283.

headlines.title: Newsom renames California labor building after Dolores Huerta
headlines.description: California Gov. Gavin Newsom is honoring the late civil rights icon Dolores Huerta by putting her name on a state building. Newsom announced Friday he will rename the new California Labor and Workforce Development Agency Building in Sacramento after the pioneer. After Huerta’s passing this week, Newsom issued a statement, saying, “We owe her an immeasurable debt of gratitude for her tireless advocacy…and every person who walks through the doors of the building will be reminded of her enduring legacy and the mission she left for us all.” The new building officially opened at the start of this year. headlines.title: Newsom highlights California's homelessness efforts during Marin County visit
headlines.description: Gov. Gavin Newsom spoke in Marin County Friday morning about a new milestone in reducing homelessness in California and expanding access to behavioral health services. The Ritter Center in San Rafael is celebrating a new $14 million health and wellness center as a result of voter-enacted Proposition 1. The center will increase capacity by 25% and put case management, housing support, food assistance and other services under one roof. Newsom said the public needs to know that the investment voters made by voting yes on the bond measure is paying off. The full report is available in the video above.

headlines.title: San Francisco prepares for coastal flooding as high tides continue
headlines.description: Coastal flood advisories across the Bay Area have been extended into the weekend, with some communities pre-staging equipment in case they need to respond to flood-prone areas. NBC Bay Area meteorologists have warned that high tides could surge nearly 2 feet above normal, potentially causing problems for public transit in San Francisco, including Muni trains. The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) is preparing equipment, including tons of sandbags that crews can deploy as needed, large sump pumps that can be placed in flooded tunnels or submerged trouble spots, and generators to power those pumps. For Muni, two potential trouble spots are its light rail station at Cesar Chavez and Illinois streets, near flood-prone Islais Creek, and the Embarcadero Street Muni tunnel, which is close to an area along the Embarcadero that floods during high tide. “High priority for us is protecting subway service,” said John Becker, SFMTA’s acting chief infrastructure officer. “Obviously, it’s a huge link across the city and also in our shared station partnership with BART. It’s a huge regional impact we could have.” High tides have already caused flooding in Marin County this week, with low-lying areas near Mill Valley inundated since Monday. San Francisco’s Embarcadero has also flooded this week. Authorities in San Mateo County announced their flood staging plans Friday. There is only a slight chance of rain in San Francisco this weekend. The coastal flooding is happening because of unusually high tide conditions. Drivers are being reminded not to drive through flooded areas because it can be difficult to determine how deep or dangerous the water may be.
